chunks: Ali, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Yahya ibn Amr ibn Kulaib, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I have settled myself upon necessitating the Hajj every year by myself or by a man from my family with my wealth.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'And you are determined upon that?' I said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If you were to do so, then receive glad tidings with the abundance of the wealth.'

key_terms.لُزُومِ: Necessitating or adhering strictly to a practice

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and material benefit of performing Hajj every year according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) responds to a companion’s resolve to perform Hajj annually, either personally or through a proxy, with the glad tidings of increased wealth. This narration highlights the Shia understanding of the material and spiritual reciprocity of consistent pilgrimage, linking the act of *Hajj* directly to divine provision (*rizq*). It underscores the merit of prioritizing religious obligations as a means to secure both worldly sustenance and spiritual elevation.
